- [testing/cases/scoped-capture.ts](/workspace/titan-nano/testing/cases/scoped-capture.ts)

The cases also check the peer’s edited file before releasing its claim, restore files under exact and parent/child scopes, and remove a file that was missing at preparation.

The negative cases detect both observed dependency changes and an unobserved peer edit. The recovery cases reuse the existing sealed-result fixture to check that restart does not repeat the original worker command.

The concurrency assertions measure runner-level windows. Exact filesystem interleavings, expanded write-baseline acceptance, and complete verification remain with the controller.

answer.evidence: The rollback cases can pass an implementation that restores the baseline and deletes worker-created files without checking whether a claimed file changed after candidate capture. The peer edits only a disjoint marker in testing/factories/scoped-capture.ts:81–101, so the conflict checks in packages/runner/src/live.ts:73–75 and the reconciliation path in packages/runner/src/file-reconciliation.ts:22–57 can regress without failing these cases. The write counters at testing/factories/scoped-capture.ts:117 and :223 bracket runner activity. They reject whole-run serialization and, with the symlink assertions, whole-project reads during preparation and rollback. They can still pass if peer writes are paused during the actual snapshot I/O and resume before the counters are checked. The sealed-result fixture does verify one original worker execution and retained receipt fields after replay. Findings are from read-only source inspection. No tests were run.

Live restore-point preparation, rollback comparison, and rollback approval hashing now capture only the negotiated write scope. Expanded write baselines already used selected paths. Full candidate and reconciliation captures remain in place because shell and native reads can observe files outside the write scope.

Changed files:

- [packages/runner/src/live.ts](/workspace/titan-nano/packages/runner/src/live.ts)
- [packages/runner/src/steps.ts](/workspace/titan-nano/packages/runner/src/steps.ts)

An unrelated changing file or symlink previously could abort a scope-only capture before the runner filtered the results. The selected-path read excludes that peer. A change outside the write scope can still invalidate a candidate, even when the phase recorded some managed reads. Whole-project claims and path lists beyond the selected-read limit still use full capture.

Biome and `git diff --check` passed. A filtered run reported 12 passing recovery cases, including sealed script recovery without a repeated command, but exited unsuccessfully at the Podman boundary guard. Podman could not initialize in this sandbox. The adversarial concurrency cases and installed-package verification remain pending with the controller. No OpenSpec acceptance was closed.

answer.evidence: Rollback fails when an outside edit replaces a parent directory with a regular file. Declare `dir/a` in the write scope, let the worker delete it and seal the candidate, then replace the empty `dir` with a regular file before rollback. The selected capture sees the parent, but `scoped` drops it. Rollback treats `dir/a` as missing in both the candidate and the live tree, then `putBack` fails while trying to create `dir`. The existing rollback logic therefore bypasses conflict reconciliation for this case. See [live.ts](/workspace/titan-nano/packages/runner/src/live.ts:68) and [workspace/index.ts](/workspace/titan-nano/packages/workspace/src/index.ts:125). The inspected live cases cover individual outside edits, and the snapshot recovery cases cover WAL mutations during full capture. Neither proves continuous unrelated writes are tolerated during scoped preparation and rollback. Source inspection confirmed that candidate verification still compares the full readable tree even when managed reads exist, and expanded write baselines still use selected paths and verify their stored hashes. `git diff --check` passed. No files were changed and no suites were run.

Live restore-point preparation, rollback, and rollback reconciliation now capture the negotiated write set. If an outside edit replaces `dir` with a regular file after the worker deletes `dir/a`, rollback reports a conflict. Approved conflict-preserving rollback leaves the replacement intact.

- [live.ts](/workspace/titan-nano/packages/runner/src/live.ts)
- [steps.ts](/workspace/titan-nano/packages/runner/src/steps.ts)
- [file-reconciliation.ts](/workspace/titan-nano/packages/runner/src/file-reconciliation.ts)

Typecheck, Biome, and `git diff --check` passed. Two temporary-filesystem probes exercised the rollback code directly. One verified restoration of an exact missing file and reproduced the parent replacement conflict. The other recorded 547 unrelated writes overlapping selected capture and rollback while the claimed file was restored. The integration run failed the required Podman boundary check, so end-to-end verification remains pending.

Candidate capture and validation still use the full readable view because shell and native reads can be unobserved even when managed reads exist. Retained reconciliation snapshots keep their full hash checks, and expanded write baselines already use selected capture. Unrestricted scopes and selections above the existing selected-path limit still use full capture. The acceptance files and delivery record were outside the writable scope. No OpenSpec tasks were closed.
